title: Picture gen with transparency?
author: Merinther
selftext:
I'm trying to generate some pictures for a game, but I'd like them to be generated with a transparent background. It would be annoying if everything in the game has to be rectangular! I want to find a free generator that can do that.

Dall-E/ChatGPT seems to work well, but only offers 1-2 images per day. Gentube looks like it does everything else I need, but no transparency. Googling just finds a bunch of background removers, which sort of do the job, but the result doesn't look great.

Do you know any better options?

comments.author: AnonymousAggregator
comments.body: Make it go a green screen background. It should be able to vibecode it out.

comments.author: Ahooovo
comments.body: I've used copilot for some basic sprites, specify you want PNG and no background

replies.author: Merinther
replies.body: Also seems to work well, but apparently it has a limit of "approximately 1-15 image generations per day"?

replies.author: Ahooovo
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/sex6080k9wng1.jpeg?width=1080&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=171a95bd472411f8837e1b4da6d63d3dcccc4c3d

This is on the Copilot app. like someone else said, there is a limit for free users, somewhere around 10 image generations per day. Just be very specific in what you want, describe it well, specify you need a PNG file and no background and it should work. If you want a character copied or a art style copied, upload a reference image and specify.

I have tried getting it to make sprite sheets or animate a sprite in different ways but haven't had luck.

replies.author: gestapov
replies.body: Interesting, nano banana 2 couldn't do it but I tried in the copilot app and it worked lol

comments.author: Weekly_Algae5902
comments.body:
i have added replicate calls to my automated workflow, there's a bunch of background removers that will return an alpha layer for you.  And the cost is really low (but watch out, some are crazy expensive).

[https://replicate.com/smoretalk/rembg-enhance](https://replicate.com/smoretalk/rembg-enhance)

  
or just run rembg on your local PC and do it on your own.

replies.author: kal101246
replies.body: Wait you can run rembg on your own PC locally without having to spend any money? Do you mind explaining how that works?

replies.author: Weekly_Algae5902
replies.body: it's a python library, pip install rembg, and then write a script to call it.

comments.body: I just as the llm for the alpha channel of the original prompt and add the original image as references and then have ai read the image and see if it makes sense.. if not redo

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for spritesheets and game art, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio (https://gamelabstudio.co). It’s designed for game assets, not just characters, and it’ll generate consistent artwork, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything: creatures, machines, towers, VFX, projectiles, etc. Animations aren’t locked to walk/idle either; you can generate attack, fire, spin, explode, transform, whatever the gameplay needs.

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

comments.author: IndubitablyNerdy
comments.body: Gimp can easily remove backgrounds (if they are plain color at least, which most models will generate if you put it in the prompt) and is free, on top of that it can help learning some image editing that might be useful anyway with game development. Photoshop can do the same ofc, but not for free.
